articles.headline: Sources: Bagent has concussion, leaving Bears' QB situation unclear
articles.description: Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is in the NFL's concussion protocol, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is in the NFL's concussion protocol, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Tuesday.

With Caleb Williams' availability for next Monday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles uncertain due to a hamstring injury, third-string quarterback Case Keenum could be in line to start. Keenum has not appeared in a regular-season NFL game since 2023.

Bagent came in at quarterback in Chicago's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday after Williams left because of his injury.

It is unclear when Bagent suffered the concussion, but he was sacked on the final play of Sunday's game when the Vikings' Dallas Turner bulldozed through tight end Colston Loveland, who was singled up with the outside linebacker.

Bagent, who has been the Bears' backup quarterback since signing with the team in 2023 as an undrafted free agent, finished Sunday's game 5-of-9 passing for 54 yards in Sunday's game.

Coach Ben Johnson said Monday that Williams is considered week-to-week with his right hamstring injury but he did not yet rule the quarterback out for the game against the Eagles even though Johnson does not expect the quarterback to practice this week.

"He's right now working through every avenue that he's got available to get back on track here. We'll see what that looks like. Here's what I know. This guy's a little bit different than the average human being. I said that last night, I'll double down on that. He gets back -- he has in the past -- a lot faster than what people can anticipate and so I'm not putting a timeline on this. We're going to say week-to-week. He's going to attack this with everything that he knows," Johnson said of Williams.

Williams underwent an MRI on Monday morning to assess the severity of his hamstring injury. Johnson said the news the Bears received on Williams' injury was "somewhat encouraging."

articles.headline: Sources: Giants QB Jaxson Dart out for extended period
articles.description: Jaxson Dart's knee injury is more severe than originally anticipated, and the Giants QB could miss the rest of the season, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
Jaxson Dart's knee injury is more severe than initially anticipated, and the New York Giants quarterback could miss the rest of the season, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.

Dart suffered the injury during the opening possession of Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Coach John Harbaugh said after the game that the Giants likely avoided a "devastating outcome" with Dart's knee.

But sources told Rapoport and Garafolo that the second-year star will miss an extended period of time and is facing the possibility of season-ending surgery.

Harbaugh said Monday that evaluations on Dart's knee were still ongoing and declined to comment further on his timeline to return.

The Giants lost Dart on their seventh snap of the game, when he was hit on his right side by Rams linebacker Byron Young. That hit sent Dart into linebacker Josaiah Stewart, who undercut the quarterback's legs, resulting in a hard fall.

Dart immediately grabbed at his left knee and went to the blue medical tent. He walked with a limp to the locker room and initially was listed as questionable to return to the game before officially being ruled out early in the third quarter.

With Dart sidelined, the Giants turned to veteran Jameis Winston, went completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.

Beyond Winston, the Giants have quarterback Jake Haener on their practice squad. But with Dart expected to miss an extended period, Harbaugh and the Giants will lean on Winston, who signed a two-year, $13 million contract extension earlier this month.

articles.headline: Nacua and Bowers lead fantasy football Knockout league pickups for Week 3
articles.description: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.
articles.body:
Injuries are the great equalizer in sports.

They can prove especially devastating in fantasy football Knockout leagues.

On Monday night, New York Giants QB Jaxson Dart became the second quarterback in as many weeks to suffer a game-ending injury within the first 11 snaps while scoring fewer than one fantasy point (0.80), joining Kyler Murray (Week 1). Unsurprisingly -- though it's worth pointing out that he was facing a difficult matchup against the Los Angeles Rams -- Dart resided on the largest percentage of teams knocked out for Week 2, with an even higher rate than anyone had the week before (19.6%).

Dart wasn't alone. Philadelphia Eagles RB Saquon Barkley, who played only 10 snaps (14% of the Eagles' total on offense) and 3.0 fantasy points, was the most commonly knocked out running back for the second consecutive week. Along with those two, the top 10 names on this week's list also included Caleb Williams and DJ Moore, who left their respective contests early due to injuries, as well as Nico Collins (hamstring), Puka Nacua (hip), Brock Bowers (knee) and A.J. Brown (ankle), all of whom were ruled out in advance of their respective games.

It's a factor in the Knockout format that'll ring louder with each passing week.

As teams get eliminated and your active managerial pool shrinks, rosters strengthen and injury-influenced lineup holes increasingly sink your team in the standings. It's something to keep in mind as you evaluate the downside risk of your weekly lineup.

Yes, some injuries can be chalked up to bum luck -- for a great historical example, no one could've foreseen Tom Brady tearing his ACL in 2008's opening week -- but others can be reasonably forecasted. In Dart's case,  we  warned  you about his downside risks, which made him a disadvantageous pick in the Knockout format.

Dart's injury underscores another critical factor for Knockout play: Stacking, as his top wide receiver, Malik Nabers, scored only 1.1 fantasy points while working most of the day with backup Jameis Winston. It's the second time in Nabers' past four games played that he has delivered a miserable, sub-four-point score terribly sunk by poor quarterback play (3.3 in Week 3 of 2025, with Russell Wilson as his quarterback). And with Tuesday's report that Dart might miss the remainder of the season, Nabers is probably looking at more low-floor scores like those. 

Tying your wide receiver's result to your quarterback's can prove dangerous, especially if either -- and in this case both -- carries an injury question.

That's not to say that you cannot stack! Outcomes like Dak Prescott's 29.76 and CeeDee Lamb's 35.3 fantasy point Week 2 working together are plenty welcome across all fantasy leagues, but remember, it's floor, not ceiling, that's the goal in Knockout play.

To that end, in the Fantasy Focus Podcast Knockout league, this week's knocked out team started both Dart and Nabers. A team projected before Monday Night Football to survive by 21.5 fantasy points

articles.headline: Sources: Jets sign ex-Titans QB Will Levis, release Bailey Zappe
articles.description: The Jets have signed former Titans starting QB Will Levis to their practice squad and have released Bailey Zappe, a source confirmed to ESPN.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets added a former starter to their quarterback room, signing Will Levis to their practice squad Tuesday, a source confirmed to ESPN.

Levis, who worked out for the Jets before Week 1, went 5-16 as the Tennessee Titans' starter in 2023 and 2024 before missing last season due to shoulder surgery.

A second-round pick (33rd overall) in 2023, Levis was considered the Titans' quarterback of the future but was undone by turnovers. He was replaced by Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in 2025.

In a corresponding move, the Jets released quarterback Bailey Zappe (nine career starts) from the practice squad. Geno Smith and rookie Cade Klubnik are on the active roster.

Levis, 27, became available when he was cut by the Titans at the end of the preseason. They decided to go with Ward and Mitchell Trubisky as their top two quarterbacks.

"There are not 32 quarterbacks in this league better than me. I know that for sure," Levis said in the preseason. "I know I've put the tape out there already that I'm a dang good quarterback in this league."

Levis showed some promise as a rookie, throwing eight touchdowns and four interceptions in nine starts. But, in 2024, he won only two of 12 starts and had almost as many interceptions (13) and touchdown passes (12), prompting then-coach Brian Callahan to bench him late in the year.

In the 2026 preseason, Levis completed 21 of 39 passes for 200 yards, with no touchdowns and no interceptions.

articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 3

Welcome to Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

Jump to a section:

Superflex rankings (with QBs)

Standard flex rankings (RBs, WRs, TEs only)

-->These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Falcons-Packers game.

-->

Week 3 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Josh Allen, QB1 vs LAC

He probably cannot average 38.2 fantasy points per game for long, but he belongs in his own tier.
 2. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 vs NYJ

As long as each Lions game is a shootout, there is nothing to worry about here.
 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 @ WSH

Perhaps last season wasn't a fluke. He is doing it again, regardless of quarterback.
 4. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 @ MIA

We have never seen him play like this before, with this much volume. Just. Stay. Healthy.
 5. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR2 vs NYJ

Nobody has more targets than this fellow. We expected more of a split with Jameson Williams.
 6. Christian McCaffrey, RB3 vs ARI

Low volume is not a concern yet, but it will be if he doesn't score touchdowns.
 7. Jonathan Taylor, RB4 vs HOU

It sure looks like last season was not a fluke for him. The touchdowns keep on coming.
 8. Lamar Jackson, QB2 @ DAL

He wasn't awesome in Week 2, but this week, it is the Cowboys. He should be awesome.
 9. Brock Purdy, QB3 vs ARI

Enjoy this week versus Arizona. Then he faces the Broncos and Seahawks.
 10. Jalen Hurts, QB4 @ CHI

The Eagles offense remains in flux, but Hurts is not a problem.
 11. Patrick Mahomes, QB5 @ MIA

 12. Tyler Shough, QB6 vs LV

 13. Puka Nacua, WR3 @ DEN

A hip injury cost him Week 2. At least the Rams don't play on Monday this week.
 14. Ja'Marr Chase, WR4 @ PIT

Magnificent player who needs to produce those Week 2 numbers more often. He needs more volume.
 15. Justin Jefferson, WR5 @ TB

 16. Chris Olave, WR6 vs LV

 17. CeeDee Lamb, WR7 vs BAL

 18. Derrick Henry, RB5 @ DAL

The Ravens underutilized him in second half last week, which makes no sense.
 19. Bijan Robinson, RB6 @ GB

Thursday is a big game for his fantasy value, but can we really doubt this guy?
 20. Dak Prescott, QB7 vs BAL

 21. Joe Burrow, QB8 @ PIT

 22. Jordan Love, QB9 vs ATL

We didn't expect to rank him so well, but quite a few backup QBs are starting this week.

Underwhelming Week 2 versus a tough opponent, so he gets a pass. But he needs to run more.
 24. De'Von Achane, RB7 vs KC

He did have 23 touches in Week 2. We cannot expect his 2025 numbers, but don't give up on him.

articles.headline: Yankees don't expect Aaron Judge (calf) back for wild card
articles.description: Aaron Judge is not expected to be available for the Yankees' wild-card series as he continues to recover from a calf strain.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Yankees manager Aaron Boone said he does not expect to have Aaron Judge available for the Wild Card series next week, though he did not completely rule out the star right fielder recovering from his calf strain in time to play.

"We're planning on him not being a part of that," Boone said Tuesday before the Yankees hosted the Tampa Bay Rays for a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.

Judge was placed on the injured list with a right calf strain Friday, two days after exiting a game against the Minnesota Twins with the injury. Judge and the team declined to specify the severity of the injury through the weekend. On Tuesday, Boone labeled it a "moderate grade" strain. He said Judge received a PPP injection Monday and will avoid physical activity over the "next couple days."

"You hear all the time with injuries, we get ranges," Boone said. "Two to four weeks, four to six, all these things. There are ranges for a reason, and we're at a point in the year where obviously we push it a little bit if that was in play. But that's a week away so I'm not expecting it, but I'm not ruling it out either."

Judge, 34, sustained the injury in his seventh game back after missing more than three months with a fractured rib. The three-time MVP returned without going on a rehab assignment and went 4-for-23 with 13 strikeouts, one walk, and one home run in 24 plate appearances. He will likely finish his injury-plagued campaign with a .241 batting average, 18 home runs and an .871 OPS in just 66 games after two historic MVP seasons.

Heliot Ramos will start in right field for the fourth straight game since Judge's absence in Tuesday's opener. Spencer Jones is another option to play right field in the postseason should Trent Grisham, who is on the injured list with a hamstring injury, return to play center field.

The Rays entered Tuesday's doubleheader with a magic number of one to clinch the American League East title with seven games remaining. Barring a Rays collapse, the Yankees will host the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card series for the second consecutive year.

articles.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's start counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

How many rookies landed in our top 100? Which stars who changed teams this summer are climbing our rankings? Where will the defending champion New York Knicks check in?

Our countdown begins with players Nos. 100-51 and continues Wednesday with Nos. 50-11 and Thursday with our expert panel's predictions for this season's top 10.

And that expert panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

100. Luguentz Dort

G | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 64

The Dorture Chamber heads southeast, where the Hawks will be downright scary on the wings with Dort, Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels. Dort is still one of the league's most physical defenders and is entering the final year of his contract (at $18.2 million), so he'll be motivated in a new environment. His 3-point shooting fell off last season after two years at a 40% clip with the Thunder. Even if last season was a regression to the mean, the physicality Dort brings is the sell for the Hawks. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Dort defended 2026 All-Stars for 1,238 matchups last season, the third most in the NBA.

Fantasy projection: 9.6 PTS, 3.8 REB, 1.0 STL

99. RJ Barrett

G | Toronto Raptors

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 100

Barrett, the No. 3 pick in the 2019 draft, is a reliable secondary scorer who creates advantages with downhill attacks and plays well off lead options. Though the Toronto native hasn't developed into a franchise wing because of his mediocre outside shot and limited defensive impact, he thrilled his hometown fans in May with the signature moment of his seven-year career. When Barrett bounced home a last-second 3-pointer to beat the Cavaliers and force Game 7 in the Raptors' first-round playoff series, fans indulged in their most raucous celebration since the 2019 championship parade. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Barrett shot 64% on layups and dunks last season, best in a season in his career and up from 55% in 2024-25, per GeniusIQ tracking.

Fantasy projection: 19.7 PTS, 5.6 REB, 3.9 AST

98. Jalen Suggs

G | Orlando Magic

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 59
